reason: Conversation 1 is essentially a non-answer: it refuses to engage, gives a generic safety line and points to an engineer without asking anything or raising the warranty, which fails the homeowner on diagnosis, questions and escalation guidance. Conversation 2 ran the sensible socket check, kept the customer away from internal electrics, surfaced the extended-warranty question and correctly routed him to Candy or an engineer rather than selling a part. Its weakness is overconfidence - calling the PCB fuse 'almost certainly' the cause and treating a surge as fact when the homeowner doesn't know, whereas the truth is genuinely uncertain between board, mains filter and wiring - but since it still steered to an engineer without recommending a purchase, this is a clear rather than decisive win for 2.
